title: Blinded seeded-overlap detection

cases.title: For drone/satellite place recognition, divide a backbone feature map into concentric square-ring parts, pool each part separately, and enforce identity learning per part so surrounding geographic context improves matching across views.
cases.expected: Each Part Matters: Local Patterns Facilitate Cross-view Geo-localization: Concentric square-ring partitioning and per-part feature learning for cross-view localization.
cases.observed: Every substantive component of B1 is explicitly present in LPN, including the square-ring geometry and separate part supervision. This is not merely a broad resemblance to part-based representation learning.

evidence.title: Each Part Matters: Local Patterns Facilitate Cross-view Geo-localization
evidence.mechanism_overlap: Local Pattern Network (LPN) partitions backbone feature maps into square rings, average-pools each part, predicts a geographic identity for each part, and minimizes the summed part-wise cross-entropy losses. Satellite and drone branches share weights. Concatenated part descriptors are used for retrieval, explicitly exploiting surrounding context.
evidence.evidence_location: Section III, especially Figure 3 and its caption, PDF page 4; partition and classifier discussion on PDF pages 4–5; abstract for contextual motivation.
evidence.quote: The network is optimized by minimizing the sum of the cross-entropy losses over all parts.

independent_verification.review_status: Independent coordinator inspected the retrieved primary text: square-ring partition, part-wise pooled features, shared satellite/drone backbone and per-part cross-entropy are explicit in Section III/Figure 3. No new retrieval mechanism is supplied by B1.

cases.title: Replace global random negatives in cross-view geographic image contrastive learning with a curriculum using geographic-neighbor hard negatives and dynamically selected feature-similarity hard negatives, retaining a simple shared image encoder.
cases.expected: Sample4Geo: Hard Negative Sampling For Cross-View Geo-Localisation: Geographic and feature-similarity hard-negative sampling for contrastive cross-view representation learning.
cases.observed: The proposed sampler curriculum and simple shared encoder are established together, not assembled retrospectively from different papers. DSS periodically refreshes neighbor distances and mixes the closest samples with randomly selected samples from the top-neighbor set.

evidence.title: Sample4Geo: Hard Negative Sampling For Cross-View Geo-Localisation
evidence.mechanism_overlap: A weight-shared ConvNeXt encoder with mean pooling and symmetric InfoNCE uses geographic near-neighbor negatives early in training, then Dynamic Similarity Sampling from current embedding cosine similarities. The paper explicitly replaces the former sampler with the latter after initial epochs.
evidence.evidence_location: Sections 3.1–3.4; PDF page 4, particularly Section 3.3 Near Neighbour Sampling Based on GPS and Section 3.4 Dynamic Similarity Sampling.
evidence.quote: After a certain amount of epochs, GPS-based sampling is replaced by our Dynamic Similarity Sampling (DSS).

independent_verification.review_status: Independent coordinator inspected Sections 3.1-3.4: shared Siamese ConvNeXt, geographic near-neighbor initialization and replacement by dynamic feature-similarity sampling are explicit. The University-1652 exception must be preserved; GPS initialization was not possible there.

cases.title: Build a drone-view localization benchmark connecting university buildings across satellite, drone, and ground photographs, evaluating drone-to-satellite target localization and satellite-to-drone navigation via image retrieval.
cases.expected: University-1652: A Multi-view Multi-source Benchmark for Drone-based Geo-localization: University-building satellite/drone/ground benchmark and bidirectional drone-satellite retrieval tasks.
cases.observed: The buildings, platforms, two query directions, and retrieval interpretation match the benchmark's defining construction. The publication is ACM Multimedia 2020, not ECCV.

evidence.title: University-1652: A Multi-view Multi-source Benchmark for Drone-based Geo-localization
evidence.mechanism_overlap: University-1652 connects 1,652 buildings from 72 universities across satellite, simulated drone, and ground views. Its two named retrieval tasks are drone-view target localization and drone navigation in the reverse query direction. The protocol uses Recall@K and average precision.

cases.title: Use a transformer-based cross-view geolocalizer that avoids explicit polar transformation and uses attention to select informative regions for a second non-uniform image sampling stage.
cases.expected: TransGeo: Transformer Is All You Need for Cross-view Image Geo-localization: Transformer cross-view localization without polar transformation and attention-guided non-uniform cropping.
cases.observed: The claimed architecture, absence of polar preprocessing, attention criterion, and second-stage non-uniform selection all coincide with TransGeo. Replacing the term cropping with sampling does not supply a mechanism difference.

evidence.title: TransGeo: Transformer Is All You Need for Cross-View Image Geo-Localization
evidence.mechanism_overlap: TransGeo uses a pure transformer without polar transformation and a two-stage attend-and-zoom-in procedure. Attention selects aerial-image patches for non-uniform cropping; computation saved by dropping patches is allocated to higher-resolution informative regions.
evidence.evidence_location: Abstract, PDF page 1; Figure 1, PDF page 3; Section 3.3 and Figure 2, PDF page 4; Table 4 and Section 4.5 ablations.
evidence.quote: We further leverage the flexibility of transformer input and propose an attention-guided non-uniform cropping method

cases.title: For robust dense two-view correspondence, use frozen pretrained visual foundation features for coarse matching with an anchor-based classification/regression formulation, then refine at finer resolution using a separate feature pyramid.
cases.expected: RoMa: Robust Dense Feature Matching: Frozen foundation features, coarse anchor-based matching and fine refinement.
cases.observed: The same paper contains the complete recipe. Section 3.3 specifies 64 by 64 classification anchors covering the image grid. This directly rejects novelty of the generic frozen-foundation coarse/independent-fine matching formulation.

evidence.title: RoMa: Robust Dense Feature Matching
evidence.mechanism_overlap: RoMa freezes DINOv2 for coarse features, decouples the fine encoder and uses VGG19 fine features, predicts a multimodal distribution over spatial classification anchors with a transformer decoder, and performs subsequent robust-regression refinement.
evidence.evidence_location: Section 3.2, PDF page 4; Section 3.3 Regression-by-Classification and Equation 8, PDF page 5; Section 3.4 losses, PDF pages 5–6; abstract.
evidence.quote: We keep the DINOv2 encoder frozen throughout training.

limitations: Five purposively chosen positive overlap cases are a smoke test, not a statistical accuracy estimate.
All cases are overlap positives; this test alone cannot measure specificity or false rejection rate.
The investigator may know these methods from training. Procedural blinding does not establish memorization-free retrieval ability.
ground_truth_corrections: Before seeing investigator output, direct source checks invalidated provisional arXiv identifiers 2107.14068 and 2303.11845: these belong to unrelated astronomy and mathematics papers. Removed and replaced with OpenAlex-verified exact DOI/title pairs.
A further attempted LPN locator 2011.14506 was also unrelated and was never accepted as evidence. These errors are a concrete demonstration of why model-memory citations cannot be trusted.
One OpenAlex query returned HTTP 429; the already-recorded successful Sample4Geo retrieval supplied the verified DOI. No label or mechanism expectation changed.
